newSounds: is a vowel made with the lips spread and the tongue pulled back, like Telugu ఇ said further back - no English equivalent, practise yh. Soft (palatalised) consonants: e//// and the soft sign make the consonant before them sound like it is said with the tongue against the palate (compare Telugu కి/గి). is a throat sound like Scottish loch or German Bach. and are always hard (zh, sh).
rhythm: Stress is strong and unpredictable - it can fall on any syllable and is not marked in normal writing, so learn each word's stress. Unstressed vowels reduce: and become a short uh, /// weaken, and saying every vowel fully sounds over-clear but is still understood.
registerFirst: (vy) is the polite 'you' - use it with strangers, officials, elders and in shops. (ty) is the informal form for family, friends and children; wait to be invited to switch. Verbs change ending to match: , .
trap: Do not read Russian as if it were Latin: stress the marked syllable every time (e.g. is spuh-SEE-buh, not SPAH-see-buh) and reduce the unstressed vowels. The first in is silent, but you can simply say Privet with friends.
